quizName: DMV Practice Test #10 30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: To help other drivers see your motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Make eye contact with other drivers.

questions.explanation: Using your headlight is the best way to help other drivers see your motorcycle. Check that your headlight works before you ride.

questions.question: How are convex mirrors different from regular mirrors?

options.text: They show a narrower view of the road.
They show a wider view of the road.
They show a clearer view of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: They show a wider view of the road.
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors are common on motorcycles. They show a wider view than flat mirrors. However, they can make vehicles behind you look farther away than they really are.

questions.question: When riding, your boots or shoes should:
questions.explanation: Your shoes should be high and sturdy to cover and support your ankles. Keep heels low so they don't catch on objects. Tuck in shoelaces so they don't get caught on the motorcycle.

questions.question: You should avoid riding directly next to another vehicle because:

options.text: The other driver may want to use your lane to pass.
You may be in the vehicle's blind spot.
You may have a route to escape.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be in the vehicle's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding next to another vehicle is dangerous. The driver may not see you if you are in their blind spot. Also, the vehicle could block your escape route if a hazard appears.

questions.question: If another driver makes eye contact with you:

options.text: You know they have seen you.
It doesn't always mean they have actually seen you.
They will give you the right of way.

questions.correctAnswerText: It doesn't always mean they have actually seen you.
questions.explanation: Do not assume eye contact means a driver has seen you. A driver can look directly at a motorcycle and still not notice it.

questions.question: Before riding, check your clutch. A working clutch should feel:
questions.explanation: Check your clutch and throttle before riding. The throttle should snap back when you release it. The clutch should feel tight and smooth.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, tell them to:

options.text: Get on the motorcycle before you start the engine.
Sit as far back as possible.

questions.explanation: Tell passengers to stay quiet and still while the motorcycle is moving. Passengers should only get on after the engine starts. They should sit as far forward as possible without getting in your way.

questions.question: You have the best chance of avoiding serious injury in a crash if you wear:
questions.explanation: A helmet is your best protection against injury. A plastic face shield that won't shatter helps protect your face in a crash.

questions.question: When it starts to rain, you should:

options.text: Ride in the tire tracks left by other vehicles.
Ride in the center of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by other vehicles.
questions.explanation: When it rains, do not ride in the center of the lane. Instead, ride in the tire tracks left by cars in front of you. The left track often works best, but this depends on traffic and conditions.

questions.question: A "wobble" in the front wheel and handlebars is usually caused by:

options.text: Incorrect tire pressure or uneven loading.
The front wheel not being fastened tightly to the frame.
Hitting an object with the front tire.

questions.correctAnswerText: Incorrect tire pressure or uneven loading.
questions.explanation: A wobble is when the front wheel and handlebars shake side to side. Most wobbles are caused by improper loading, wrong accessories, or incorrect tire pressure.

questions.question: What is a good way to handle a tailgater?

options.text: Slow down or change lanes to let the tailgater pass.
Speed up to get away from the tailgater.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down or change lanes to let the tailgater pass.
questions.explanation: If it is safe, change lanes and let the tailgater pass. Speeding up will not help. The tailgater may just follow you at a higher speed, which is more dangerous.

questions.question: Where is there the greatest risk of conflict between you and other vehicles?
questions.explanation: Intersections have the greatest potential for conflict between motorcycles and other vehicles.

questions.question: When stopping your motorcycle with a passenger, what should you do?

options.text: Ride a little faster than usual.
Start slowing down earlier than usual.
Merge into smaller traffic gaps than usual.

questions.correctAnswerText: Start slowing down earlier than usual.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight to your motorcycle. The extra weight makes the motorcycle slower to respond. It takes longer to speed up, slow down, and turn. Start slowing earlier, reduce your speed, and look for larger gaps in traffic.

questions.question: Under good conditions, what is the recommended minimum distance between you and the vehicle ahead?
questions.explanation: Under normal conditions, keep at least two seconds of distance between you and the vehicle ahead. Increase this distance when conditions are not ideal.

questions.question: How much stopping power does the front brake supply on a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides about three-quarters of the motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: How many alcoholic drinks affect your ability to ride safely?
questions.explanation: Even one alcoholic drink can affect your ability to ride safely. Never ride after drinking any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Vehicles will be entering the roadway.
Stop completely and proceed when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely and proceed when it is safe.
questions.explanation: Red octagonal signs are always stop signs. You must come to a complete stop, check for other traffic and pedestrians, and go only when it is safe.

questions.question: When riding in a group, how should riders be positioned?
questions.explanation: A staggered formation is best for group riding. It keeps riders close together while giving each rider enough space. Use single-file when turning, on curves, entering or exiting highways.

questions.question: What should you do when changing lanes?

options.text: Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder.
Check your mirrors. Look over your shoulder only if you see something unusual.
Either check your mirrors or look over your shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors and look over your shoulder to make sure no vehicle is in your path.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Yellow signs with black symbols warn about upcoming road conditions. This sign warns that a railroad crossing is ahead.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs have black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about upcoming road conditions. This sign warns you that a stop sign is coming.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT help prevent serious injury in a crash?
questions.explanation: A DOT-approved helmet protects your head and neck in a crash. A leather or sturdy jacket also protects you. A sweatshirt does not provide adequate protection.

questions.question: A motorized scooter can be operated with:
questions.explanation: In California, anyone with any type of driver license can operate a motorized scooter.

questions.question: When alcohol and drugs are used together, the effects:

options.text: Are less dangerous than using either one alone.
Can be stronger than using either one alone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can be stronger than using either one alone.
questions.explanation: Many drugs, including prescription and over-the-counter medicines, can make riding unsafe. When combined with alcohol, these drugs become even more dangerous.

questions.question: What does an integrated braking system do?

options.text: It connects the front and rear brakes when you apply the rear brake.
It automatically brakes based on your riding habits.
It applies the brake when you downshift gears.

questions.correctAnswerText: It connects the front and rear brakes when you apply the rear brake.
questions.explanation: Some motorcycles have integrated braking systems. When you use the rear brake pedal, it connects the front and rear brakes together. Check your owner's manual to learn how your motorcycle's brakes work.

questions.question: When entering a turn, you should:
questions.explanation: Reduce your speed before you enter a turn. Going too fast in a turn can make you slide out of your lane or off the road.

questions.question: Grabbing the front brake or pushing hard on the rear brake:

options.text: Is the best way to stop in an emergency.
Is the best way to slow down in wet conditions.

questions.explanation: Grabbing the front brake or pushing hard on the rear brake can lock the brakes. This can cause you to lose control of your motorcycle.

questions.question: If a motorcycle is towing a trailer, the following distance should:
questions.explanation: When towing a trailer, increase your following distance. The extra weight means you need more time to stop than normal.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are white with red and black markings. They tell drivers about traffic laws in that area. This sign means U-turns are not allowed.

questions.question: A sign that your front tire is flat is when steering suddenly feels:
questions.explanation: If steering suddenly feels heavy, your front tire may be flat. Stop riding and check your tires right away.
